source_acquisition.search_note: The inventory row is no_public_source_found and corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-51378f92df54/ is empty. The PDF has no author code URL and its reproducibility statement says source code is planned for release. gh searches for the exact title and LongWriter-Zero found no exact author visual repository. THUDM/LongWriter is retained because its README directly links LongWriter-Zero and arXiv:2506.18841, but its verified main tree contains no plot, figure, table, LaTeX, diagram, SVG, notebook, or current-paper visual data files; its README images and evaluation/training scripts are not treated as visual sources.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Vector training plots consistently use blue/orange/green setup colors; Figure 4 adds pale dashed baseline colors, Figure 5 uses blue/lavender/apricot outcome colors, and Figure 1 uses an illustrative pastel palette. Color carries most categorical meaning and is not systematically duplicated by shape or texture.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figures 2–4 are vector plots; Figures 1, 5, and 6 are raster images embedded in the PDF. Tables and captions are PDF text/vector rules.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman body/captions and DejaVu Sans chart labels form a recognizable system, but table body sizes range from about 6 to 10 pt, raster figures use their own typography, and inset versus page-width objects vary substantially.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: SFT vs. RL in long-form generation.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue-gray robot, cream paper, brown outlines, orange clothing, pale cream panels, and light-blue accents distinguish the cartoon objects; the semantic contrast is SFT versus RL rather than a numeric scale.

encodings.color: Illustrative object colors separate robot, person, paper, and candy motifs
encodings.line: Dotted separator and bottom bracket stage the two process states
encodings.text: Supervised Fine-tuning; Reinforcement learning; Ultra-Long text generation

figures.data_and_statistics: No quantitative data, axes, or uncertainty. The short paper strip and tug-of-war represent synthetic-data SFT, while the long scroll and finish flag represent RL-enabled ultra-long generation.
figures.evidence_relation: On p. 1 the cartoon introduces the SFT-versus-RL contrast; p. 2 cites Figure 1 before connecting fixed synthetic outputs to reward-driven GRPO and the three reward components.
design_strengths: Immediate two-state contrast before the quantitative results
Direct labels make the intended training/output mapping legible
Repeated robot motif gives the two states a consistent visual anchor
design_weaknesses: Metaphor does not expose GRPO, reward models, or data provenance
Greater scroll length can be mistaken for a quality guarantee
Raster illustration typography is disconnected from the chart/table system
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched conceptual panels to state the training-regime contrast, then follow with a computable mechanism and measured outcome.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: RL Training curves of three setups (Base-nothink, Base-think, and Continual-Pretrain-think) across three metrics: Writing RM (left), Length RM (middle), and Mean Non-Overlong Generation Length (right).

color.semantic_mapping: Blue=Continual-Pretrain-think, orange=Base-think, green=Base-nothink in all three panels.

encodings.y: Writing RM, Length RM, and mean non-overlong generation length, one metric per panel
encodings.facet: Three aligned metric panels from left to right
encodings.text: Panel y-axis labels and repeated three-item legends

figures.data_and_statistics: Three setup trajectories per panel. Writing RM is plotted on roughly 0–1, Length RM on roughly 0.2–1.0, and mean non-overlong generation length on roughly 500–3000. Semi-transparent bands surround the curves, but neither caption nor body identifies them as SD, SE, quantiles, or across-seed ranges.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2 joins the Length/Writing/Format reward design, Think Prompt, and continual-pretraining setups. The p. 5 result paragraph reads the green and orange curves for reward/Think effects; p. 6 reads the blue curve for CP before Figure 3 moves to Arena-Write Elo.
design_strengths: Shared Step axis enables parallel trajectory reading
Stable three-color identity links the same setups across panels and later figures
Reward and output-length diagnostics are placed in one evidence object
Vector rendering keeps fine curves and grid lines sharp
design_weaknesses: Repeated legends consume lower-right plot area
Different y units prevent direct visual magnitude comparison
Band semantics, seed count, and aggregation unit are absent
Displayed trajectories extend beyond the described 150-step final pipeline without explanation
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned small multiples with a common training axis and fixed series colors for mechanism diagnostics; define the band statistic in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Elo scores evaluated on Arena-Write during training for the three setups: Base-nothink, Base-think, and Continual-Pretrain-think. The y-axis shows the Elo score, and the x-axis represents training steps.

figures.data_and_statistics: Arena-Write Elo checkpoint values are shown as a single trajectory for each setup: CP-think starts above 1000 and reaches about 1400, Base-think approaches about 1200, and Base-nothink remains around 700. No seed, Elo update rule, sample size, or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: The p. 6 RQ3 result uses Figure 3 to support a higher CP RL ceiling and the near-80% win-rate interpretation. It extends Figure 2 from reward proxies to the downstream Arena-Write metric and precedes Table 1’s final benchmark summary.
design_strengths: Checkpoint dots distinguish sampled evaluations from the connecting line
Single Elo scale directly answers the RQ3 comparison
Setup colors match Figure 2 and Table 1 variants
design_weaknesses: Line interpolation can imply continuous progress between sparse checkpoints
Lower-right legend covers part of the low-score region
No uncertainty or task-level distribution is available
The chart does not state whether the plotted steps are the evaluated final-model checkpoints
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a training trajectory with one downstream preference metric using explicit checkpoint markers and the same setup/color vocabulary.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Arena-Write performance across RL training steps, comparing RL (solid) and SFT (dashed) starting from Base (orange) and Continual Pretrain (blue) initializations.

color.semantic_mapping: Solid blue/orange curves are RL from Continual Pretrain/Base; pale blue/orange dashed lines are the corresponding SFT baselines.

encodings.shape: Circular markers on RL trajectories; no markers on SFT baselines
encodings.text: Direct endpoint labels 964 and 971 for the SFT baselines

figures.data_and_statistics: Solid curves show RL scores across steps; dashed horizontal lines show fixed SFT values. The text reports SFT Base=964, SFT Continual Pretrain=971, RL Base≈1221, and RL Continual Pretrain≈1447. No uncertainty or repeated SFT measurements are represented.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 3.3 uses Figure 4 as the direct SFT-versus-RL ablation. The dashed baselines connect to the `w/o` rows in Table 1 and the same-scale synthetic-data SFT comparison in Appendix Table 4.
design_strengths: Solid/dashed line style redundantly identifies RL/SFT while color identifies initialization
Endpoint values reduce the need to estimate dashed lines from the axis
Compact inset is adjacent to the SFT vs. RL text
design_weaknesses: A fixed SFT value drawn across the full step axis can look like a time series
Training data, optimization budget, and compute parity are absent
Pale dashed colors have weak contrast in projection or grayscale
No variability is shown for either trajectory or baseline
figures.reusable_pattern: Overlay a fixed baseline with a training trajectory using orthogonal color and line-style encodings, and label whether the baseline is a single endpoint.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Win-rate results of LongWriter-Zero in human-in-the-loop win-rate evaluation. Left six charts: Outcomes judged by GPT-4.1 against six baselines (Llama-4-Scout, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, Claude-Sonnet-4, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen3-235B-A22B). Right two charts: Outcomes judged by human annotators (comparing against DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-235B-A22B). The percentage in the center indicates the overall win rate, with ties counted as 0.5 wins for each side.

color.semantic_mapping: Deep blue=Our wins, lavender=Opponent wins, pale apricot=Tie, dark red dashed line=automatic-versus-human judge separator.

encodings.line: Dashed red vertical separator between judge groups
encodings.facet: 2×4 grid: six GPT-4.1 comparisons and two human comparisons
encodings.text: Panel titles and center tie-adjusted win-rate percentages

figures.data_and_statistics: Eight donuts encode our wins, opponent wins, and ties. Center values are 98.2%, 85.5%, 72.7%, 84.4%, 67.2%, 62.8%, 62.4%, and 61.0%; the first six are GPT-4.1 judgments and the final two are human judgments. Ties count as 0.5 wins per side. The figure omits raw counts and denominators despite the text describing nearly 200 real-world queries and swapped response order.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 3.4 uses Figure 5 to complement Table 1’s single-critic absolute scores with pairwise preferences. Appendix A.5 supplies the judge prompt, order swap, and five verdict categories; Figure 5 therefore carries the automatic/human headline but not the full audit trail.
design_strengths: Eight comparisons fit into a compact repeated layout
A single legend stabilizes the three outcome meanings
The vertical divider makes judge provenance visible
Center percentages provide an immediate aggregate summary
design_weaknesses: Donut angles are difficult to compare precisely across panels
Raw counts, denominators, and uncertainty are absent
Color is the only outcome encoding and is not grayscale-safe
Aggregate percentages hide query-level heterogeneity and judge-selection effects
figures.reusable_pattern: Use repeated composition panels only with a fixed category vocabulary, shared legend, direct aggregate labels, and a companion count/denominator table.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Evolution of the "thinking" token length during RL training. The continually pretrained model consistently generates a longer reasoning chain.

encodings.line: One solid trajectory per setup with a shaded band

figures.data_and_statistics: The two curves rise and plateau, with CP-think consistently somewhat longer than Base-think. Shaded bands are visible but their statistic is not defined; the mean’s query and seed aggregation are also omitted.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 3.5 uses Figure 6 to explain the saturation of long CoT in writing, linking the Think Prompt in §2.3 to Figure 2’s training diagnostics and the context-capacity limitation discussed in the text.
design_strengths: Only two relevant setups are retained, avoiding Figure 2’s three-panel density
Rise, plateau, and small gap are easy to see
Caption states the directional finding directly
design_weaknesses: Band definition and sample granularity are missing
Rasterized plot and large axis label reduce reuse flexibility
Context cost and quality gain are not plotted together, so saturation remains a prose interpretation
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a two-series dynamic plot for a mechanism claim, but define the mean, band, and saturation criterion in the caption.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: WritingBench performance of different LLMs across six domains and three writing requirements (scale: 1–10). The domains are: (D1) Academic & Engineering, (D2) Finance & Business, (D3) Politics & Law, (D4) Literature & Art, (D5) Education, and (D6) Advertising & Marketing. Requirements include (R1) Style, (R2) Format, and (R3) Length. “C” denotes the category-specific score. Arena-Write Elo scores are shown in the final red box.

tables.uncertainty: None. WritingBench critic scores and Arena-Write Elo are point aggregates; no SD, SE, interval, sample count, or failure column is provided.
tables.data_and_statistics: Avg, ZH/EN, six domain scores D1–D6, three requirement scores R1/R2/R3 with category-specific C columns, and final Arena-Write Elo. LongWriter-Zero is Avg=8.69 and Elo=1447; it leads five of six domains while Literature & Art trails DeepSeek-R1, and its D6 score is tied. Values are shown to one decimal except Elo integers.
tables.evidence_relation: After benchmark setup, p. 7 invokes Table 1 for the highest overall critic score and domain/requirement comparisons. The `w/o Continual Pretrain` and `w/o Thinking` rows connect Figure 2–3 setups to the ablation, while Figure 4 supplies the dynamic SFT/RL view.
design_strengths: Two-level grouped header aligns global, language, domain, requirement, and Elo views
Performance and pairwise metrics share one decision surface
Bold best cells and the tinted Elo column make the focal row findable
design_weaknesses: 17×17 density and approximately 6 pt body text make cell-level reading expensive
Critic scores, category scores, and Elo use different scales in one grid
No task-level distribution, sample size, uncertainty, or failure count
Tinted Elo column has limited grayscale contrast
tables.reusable_pattern: Use grouped headers and direction indicators to align complementary metrics, but move excess slices to a readable supplement instead of compressing the main table.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.uncertainty: None. Percentages describe corpus allocation, not uncertainty estimates.
tables.data_and_statistics: Long_zh_fiction 40%, Long_en 30%, Long_zh_nonfiction 15%, Online_information 8%, Long_finance 5%, Long_essay 1%, and Ours_think 1%, summing to 100%. Descriptions identify fiction/non-fiction, web information, finance, academic papers, and Base-think-generated CoT; A.4 additionally states deduplication, language filtering, 32,768-token truncation, and Common Crawl sourcing except Ours_think.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 2 is the Appendix A.4 implementation interface for p. 6’s RQ3 continual-pretraining recipe. The 1% Ours_think row qualifies the claim that CP is only a writing corpus by exposing distilled CoT as a second change.
design_strengths: Percentages are explicit and sum to a checkable 100%
Description column keeps corpus categories interpretable
Page-width layout avoids wrapping long category names
design_weaknesses: Percentages do not provide absolute token counts or post-filter sizes
No corpus dates, contamination check, or detailed Ours_think selection
Preprocessing and provenance still require the surrounding A.4 text
tables.reusable_pattern: Put category, allocation, and semantic description in a compact booktabs table; add absolute counts and provenance for reproducibility.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: LongWriter-Zero-14B achieves strong gains at smaller scale. Even at 14B parameters, our RL framework produces substantial improvements in both absolute critic scores (WritingBench) and pairwise preference evaluations (ArenaWriter ELO).

tables.uncertainty: None. The table reports two point rows with no seed, interval, sample-size, or training-cost information.
tables.data_and_statistics: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct scores 7.60 WritingBench and 744 ArenaWriter ELO; LongWriter-Zero-14B scores 8.49 (+0.89) and 1198 (+454). WritingBench uses two decimals while ELO remains integer.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix A.7 extends the 32B headline in Table 1/Figure 4 to one 14B model and baseline, supporting a limited cross-scale robustness claim; it is not called out as a primary main-text object.
design_strengths: Two-row comparison is easy to scan
Absolute values and parenthesized gains appear together
Up arrows state the preferred direction
design_weaknesses: One smaller scale cannot establish a scale trend
ArenaWriter naming differs from Arena-Write in the main text
Fairness of data, compute, and training conditions is not represented
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact scale-extension table for one controlled size check, accompanied by training-budget and variability metadata.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: LongWriter-on-32B SFT baseline. We evaluate Qwen2.5-32B trained with LongWriter synthetic data against our LongWriter-Zero-32B. Our RL pipeline achieves substantial improvements on both WritingBench and ArenaWriter ELO.

tables.uncertainty: None. Final WritingBench and ArenaWriter ELO points have no uncertainty, sample count, step, or compute-parity field.
tables.data_and_statistics: Qwen2.5-32B (LongWriter-SFT)=8.08/964; LongWriter-Zero-32B=8.69 (+0.61)/1447 (+483). WritingBench values use two decimals and ELO values are integers.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix A.8 makes the synthetic-data SFT baseline used to interpret §3.3 Figure 4 explicit at 32B scale. It supplies a final-point check rather than the training dynamics shown in Figure 4.
design_strengths: Same-scale rows and same metrics keep the comparison focused
Parenthesized improvements make the directional result immediate
Caption names the synthetic-data baseline and target model
design_weaknesses: Only final points are shown, so training behavior cannot be checked
SFT data amount, epochs, hyperparameters, and compute are omitted
ArenaWriter spelling differs from Arena-Write
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a two-row same-scale baseline table with explicit delta columns or parentheses, while keeping fairness conditions adjacent.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: LongBench-Write results. Baseline scores follow Bai et al. (2025). LongWriter-Zero-32B obtains the best overall quality (S̄), long-horizon structure (S_l), and content quality (S_q).

tables.uncertainty: None. Baseline and LongWriter-Zero scores are point values with no uncertainty, sample size, or per-task failure column.
tables.data_and_statistics: S̄, S_l, and S_q are LongBench-Write aggregate metrics. LongWriter-Zero-32B is 86.3/84.2/88.4 and is bold in all three columns; baseline values are reported as following Bai et al. (2025) rather than as a fully re-evaluated set.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix A.9 tests transfer from WritingBench to the independent LongBench-Write benchmark. It extends Table 1 with an external metric set and sits alongside the scale and synthetic-SFT checks in Tables 3–4.
design_strengths: Metric direction is compact and the final method row is separated by a rule
Bold values make the best row immediately findable
Small table is suitable for a supplementary benchmark extension
design_weaknesses: S̄/S_l/S_q definitions depend on surrounding text or the prior benchmark paper
Baseline scores are inherited from Bai et al. (2025), limiting re-evaluation provenance
Approximately 6.7 pt body text and no uncertainty reduce auditability
tables.reusable_pattern: For a transfer benchmark, use stable metric columns, arrows, and a separated method row while marking whether baselines were recomputed or inherited.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the SFT/RL contrast; Figure 2 shows reward and length trajectories; Figure 3 maps setups to Elo; Table 1 gives the main benchmark; Figure 4 overlays SFT and RL; Figure 5 adds automatic and human pairwise outcomes; Figure 6 explains Think-length saturation; Tables 2–5 add corpus, scale, synthetic-SFT, and LongBench evidence.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure captions are mostly descriptive and define setups, axes, or judge groups without bold headline titles. Figure 6 and Tables 3–5 state directional findings; Figure 2 and Figure 6 leave shaded-band semantics unspecified, and all figures omit seed/denominator details.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 uses a two-level Models/Avg/Languages/Domains/Requirements/Elo header; Tables 2–5 use simple headers with arrows where higher is preferred. C, S̄, S_l, S_q, and ArenaWriter/Arena-Write require surrounding text or prior-paper context.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 aligns the three reward/Think/CP setups; Figure 3 adds downstream Elo; Table 1 gives final and w/o rows; Figure 4 supplies the explicit SFT/RL ablation; Figure 6 supplies Think-length dynamics. Table 2 exposes the CP recipe, while Tables 3–5 extend scale, baseline, and benchmark transfer.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main text points to Appendix A.4 for CP data, A.5 for the win-rate prompt, A.10 for case studies, and A.7–A.9 for additional tables. The appendix makes implementation boundaries inspectable but leaves the headline evidence dependent on cross-page reading.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman is stable in body, captions, and tables; DejaVu Sans is stable in vector chart labels. Figure 1/5/6 raster fonts are estimated, and table sizing varies from approximately 6 pt in dense grids to 10 pt in appendix tables.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/orange/green consistently identify setups in Figures 2–4 and 6; Figure 4 adds line-style redundancy, while Figure 5 changes to outcome colors. No global tie/ours palette or grayscale-safe redundant encoding is used.

most_reusable_patterns: Start with a matched conceptual contrast, then reuse one setup/color vocabulary across aligned mechanism curves, downstream Elo, and SFT/RL comparisons.
Use a grouped main-result header to align overall, language, domain, requirement, and independent preference metrics, with explicit arrows and units.
Separate automatic and human pairwise panels with a shared legend and tie rule, while publishing raw counts and denominators beside the aggregate chart.
Use appendix tables for recipe provenance, scale robustness, same-scale baselines, and external benchmark transfer, and mark inherited versus recomputed values.
highest_value_objects: Table 1: broadest main-result slicing and joint critic/Elo decision surface.
Figure 2: common-step mechanism view for reward, Think, and CP setups.
Figure 4: most direct visual SFT-versus-RL ablation.
failure_patterns: No explanation for curves extending beyond the described 150-step final pipeline.
Very small table text, especially Table 1 and Table 5.
Donut aggregates omit raw counts, denominators, and uncertainty.
Arena-Write/ArenaWriter naming and S̄/S_l/S_q definitions are not fully stable across captions and tables.
Color is not consistently backed by shape, line style, or grayscale-safe encoding.
No verified public plot/table/LaTeX source files were found.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper layers a conceptual SFT/RL cartoon, color-consistent training curves, a grouped benchmark table, donut preference panels, and appendix extensions to advance its RL-only long-text claim, but undefined bands, missing denominators/seeds, and absent visual source code limit auditability.
